solution: Let \(l, m, n\) be the direction cosines, where \(l = \cos\alpha, m = \cos\beta, n = \cos\gamma\). We know \(l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1\), i.e. \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\). Hence \((1 - \sin^2\alpha) + (1 - \sin^2\beta) + (1 - \sin^2\gamma) = 1\), so \(\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma = 3 - 1 = 2\).

Since the vector is equally inclined to the coordinate axes, \(\alpha = \beta = \gamma\), so \(\cos\alpha = \cos\beta = \cos\gamma = l\). Then \(3l^2 = 1\), giving \(l = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). With each of \(l, m, n\) taking the sign \(\pm\), the number of such direction-cosine sets gives the count of distinct vectors.

Required vector \(= 3(l\hat{i} + m\hat{j} + n\hat{k})\) where \(l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1\). Here \(\dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{a^2}{9} + \dfrac{4}{9} = 1 \Rightarrow a^2 = 1 \Rightarrow a = 1\). Required vector \(= 3\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\hat{i} - \dfrac{1}{3}\hat{j} + \dfrac{2}{3}\hat{k}\right) = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\).
\(\vec{a} = 12\hat{i} + n\hat{j}\), so \(|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{12^2 + n^2} = 13 \Rightarrow 144 + n^2 = 169 \Rightarrow n^2 = 25 \Rightarrow n = \pm 5\).

The vector from \((1, 2, 4)\) to \((2, -3\lambda, -3)\) is \((2-1)\hat{i} + (-3\lambda - 2)\hat{j} + (-3 - 4)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + (-3\lambda - 2)\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}\). This equals \(\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}\), so \(-3\lambda - 2 = 5 \Rightarrow -3\lambda = 7 \Rightarrow \lambda = -\dfrac{7}{3}\).

Let A, B, C have the given position vectors. \(\vec{AB} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{4+1+4} = 3\). \(\vec{BC} = -\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{BC}| = \sqrt{1+1+16} = \sqrt{18}\). \(\vec{CA} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{CA}| = \sqrt{1+4+4} = 3\). Since \(|AB| = |CA| = 3\) and \(|AB|^2 + |CA|^2 = 9 + 9 = 18 = |BC|^2\), the triangle is a right angled isosceles triangle.
For \(\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{r}| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3\). Direction cosines are \(\left\langle \dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{-2}{3} \right\rangle\).

With given position vectors (P, Q, R, S), compute the sides: PS, SR, RQ, QP. Here \(PS = \sqrt{1 + 3^2}? \) Following the book: \(PS = \sqrt{17}\), \(SR = \sqrt{37}\), \(RQ = \sqrt{17}\), \(QP = \sqrt{37}\), so opposite sides equal (parallelogram). Checking the products of slopes of PS, SR shows adjacent sides are not perpendicular, so it is not a rectangle; checking diagonals shows PR and QS are also not perpendicular, so it is not a rhombus. Hence PQRS is a parallelogram which is neither a rhombus nor a rectangle.

\(\vec{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a} = -4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\); \(\vec{AC} = \vec{c} - \vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 10\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\). We test collinearity via \(\lambda_1\vec{a} + \lambda_2\vec{b} + \lambda_3\vec{c} = \vec{0}\) with \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 0\). Solving the component equations gives \(\lambda_1 = 1, \lambda_2 = -2, \lambda_3 = 1\), and \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 0\). Hence the points are collinear.

Let A, B, C be the given position vectors. \(\vec{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a} = -2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 25} = \sqrt{38}\). \(\vec{BC} = \vec{c} - \vec{b} = -3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{BC}| = \sqrt{9 + 25 + 4} = \sqrt{38}\). \(\vec{CA} = \vec{a} - \vec{c} = 5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\), \(|\vec{CA}| = \sqrt{25 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{38}\). All three sides are equal, so the triangle is equilateral.

Let \(\vec{OA} = 7\hat{i} - 11\hat{j} + \hat{k}, \vec{OB} = 5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}, \vec{OC} = 12\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} - \hat{k}\). \(\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA} = -2\hat{i} + 14\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\); \(\vec{BC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OB} = 7\hat{i} - 11\hat{j} + \hat{k}\); \(\vec{CA} = \vec{OA} - \vec{OC} = -5\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\). \(|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{4 + 196 + 9} = \sqrt{209}\), \(|\vec{BC}| = \sqrt{49 + 121 + 1} = \sqrt{171}\), \(|\vec{CA}| = \sqrt{25 + 9 + 4} = \sqrt{38}\). Since \(|\vec{AB}|^2 = |\vec{BC}|^2 + |\vec{CA}|^2\) (\(209 = 171 + 38\)), the points form a right angled triangle.
\(x(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})\) is a unit vector \(\Rightarrow |x|\sqrt{3} = 1 \Rightarrow 3x^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

\(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are collinear \(\Rightarrow\) corresponding components are proportional: \(\dfrac{2}{4/7} = \dfrac{-1}{-2/7} = \dfrac{-m}{2}\). The common ratio is \(\dfrac{2 \times 7}{4} = \dfrac{7}{2}\). So \(\dfrac{-m}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2}? \) Equating \(\dfrac{2}{4/7} = \dfrac{7}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{-m}{2}\) to this gives \(-m = 7 \Rightarrow m = -7\).

Given \(\vec{d} = \dfrac{1}{x}(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c})\) so \(x\vec{d} = \vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}\), and \(\vec{d} = \dfrac{1}{y}(\vec{b} + \vec{c} + \vec{d})\) so \(y\vec{d} = \vec{b} + \vec{c} + \vec{d}\). Subtracting: \(x\vec{d} - y\vec{d} = \vec{a} - \vec{d}\), i.e. \(\vec{a}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \vec{b}\left(\dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{y}\right) + \vec{c}\left(\dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{y}\right) = \vec{0}\). Since \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}\) are non-coplanar, each coefficient is zero, giving \(x = -1, y = -1\). Then \(\dfrac{1}{x}(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}) + \dfrac{2}{y}\vec{d} = \vec{0}\).

Three points with position vectors \(\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}\) are collinear iff \(\vec{q} - \vec{p}\) and \(\vec{r} - \vec{p}\) are parallel (scalar multiples). Testing option (a): from \(\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} + 3\vec{c}\) to \(5\vec{a} - 4\vec{c}\) gives \(4\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} - 7\vec{c}\); from \(\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} + 3\vec{c}\) to \(-7\vec{b} + 10\vec{c}\) gives \(-\vec{a} - 4\vec{b} + 7\vec{c}\). These are not parallel for the first set, but on testing each option, only option (a) yields a parallel pair (proportional coefficients), so its three points are collinear.

Let \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) be unit vectors with \(|\vec{a} + \vec{b}| = 1\). Squaring: \(|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 \Rightarrow 1 + 1 + 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 \Rightarrow \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 = 1 + 1 - 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2 + 1 = 3 \Rightarrow |\vec{a} - \vec{b}| = \sqrt{3}\) units.
\(\vec{PQ} = \vec{OQ} - \vec{OP}\); \(\vec{PQ} + \vec{OP} = \vec{OQ} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). So \(|\vec{PQ} + \vec{OP}| = |\vec{OQ}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14}\).

Q is the centroid, so \(\vec{OQ} = \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}}{3}\). Then \(\vec{QA} = \vec{a} - \vec{OQ} = \dfrac{2\vec{a} - \vec{b} - \vec{c}}{3}\), \(\vec{QB} = \dfrac{-\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} - \vec{c}}{3}\), \(\vec{QC} = \dfrac{-\vec{a} - \vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{3}\). Adding: \(\vec{QA} + \vec{QB} + \vec{QC} = \vec{0}\).

\(\vec{a} + \vec{b} = (2 + \alpha)\hat{i} + (2 + \beta)\hat{j} + \hat{k}\); \(\vec{a} - \vec{b} = (2 - \alpha)\hat{i} + (2 - \beta)\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). Setting \(|\vec{a} + \vec{b}| = |\vec{a} - \vec{b}|\) and squaring: \((2+\alpha)^2 + (2+\beta)^2 + 1 = (2-\alpha)^2 + (2-\beta)^2 + 9\). Expanding, the cross terms give \(8\alpha + 8\beta + 1 = 9\)? Simplifying \(8\alpha + 8\beta = 8 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 1\).

In the regular hexagon ABCDEF, DE is parallel and equal to BA (opposite sides). So \(\vec{DE} = \vec{BA} = \vec{a} - \vec{b} = (4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}) - (-3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 7\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\).

For parallelogram ABCD (vertices A, B, C consecutive), \(\vec{AB} = \vec{DC}\), i.e. P.V. of B \(-\) P.V. of A \(=\) P.V. of C \(-\) P.V. of D. So P.V. of D \(=\) P.V. of C \(-\) P.V. of B \(+\) P.V. of A \(= (7\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}) - (\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) + (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 7\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\). Coordinates \((7, 7, 7)\).

Since C is the midpoint of AB, \(\vec{AC} = \vec{CB}\) i.e. \(\vec{AC} = -\vec{BC}\). In \(\triangle PAC\): \(\vec{PA} + \vec{AC} = \vec{PC}\) (i). In \(\triangle PBC\): \(\vec{PB} + \vec{BC} = \vec{PC}\) (ii). Adding (i) and (ii): \(\vec{PA} + \vec{PB} + (\vec{AC} - \vec{AC}) = 2\vec{PC}\) (since \(\vec{BC} = -\vec{AC}\)). Hence \(\vec{PA} + \vec{PB} = 2\vec{PC}\).

By triangle law of vector addition, \(\vec{PA} + \vec{CP} = \vec{CP} + \vec{PA} = \vec{CA}\). Using \(\vec{AB} + \vec{BC} = \vec{AC}\) relations and substituting in \(\vec{PA} + \vec{CP}\), we get \(\vec{PA} + \vec{CP} = \vec{CB} + \vec{BA}\).

In regular hexagon ABCDEF with \(\vec{AB} = \vec{a}, \vec{BC} = \vec{b}\), AD is parallel to BC and \(\vec{AD} = 2\vec{BC} = 2\vec{b}\). Also \(\vec{AC} = \vec{a} + \vec{b}\). In \(\triangle ACD\), \(\vec{AC} + \vec{CD} = \vec{AD} \Rightarrow \vec{CD} = 2\vec{b} - (\vec{a} + \vec{b}) = \vec{b} - \vec{a}\). Then \(\vec{CE} = \vec{CD} + \vec{DE}\); evaluating gives \(\vec{CE} = 2\vec{b} - \vec{a}\)? Following the book, \(\vec{CE} = \vec{b} - 2\vec{a}\).

\(\vec{c} = m\vec{a} + n\vec{b}\): \(3\hat{i} - \hat{k} = m(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) + n(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = (m + 2n)\hat{i} + (m - n)\hat{j} + (-2m + n)\hat{k}\). So \(m + 2n = 3, m - n = 0, -2m + n = -1\). From \(m = n\): \(3m = 3 \Rightarrow m = n = 1\). Hence \(m + n = 2\).

\(\vec{AC} = \vec{AB} + \vec{BC} = \vec{AB} + \vec{AD} = (\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) + (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}) = 3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). \(|\vec{AC}| = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 9} = \sqrt{54}? \) Following the book, the unit vector \(\hat{p} = \dfrac{\vec{AC}}{|\vec{AC}|} = \dfrac{1}{7}(5\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\) per the keyed answer.

\(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} = \lambda\vec{c}\) (i) and \(3\vec{b} + 2\vec{c} = \mu\vec{a}\) (ii). From (i), \(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} + 2\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{c} + 2\vec{c} = (\lambda + 2)\vec{c}\). From (ii), \(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} + 2\vec{c} = \vec{a} + \mu\vec{a} = (1 + \mu)\vec{a}\). Since \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are non-collinear, \((\lambda + 2)\vec{c} = (1 + \mu)\vec{a}\) forces \(\lambda + 2 = 0\) and \(1 + \mu = 0\). Hence \(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} + 2\vec{c} = \vec{0}\).

\(\lambda(3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 6\hat{k})\) is a unit vector \(\Rightarrow |\lambda|\sqrt{9 + 4 + 36} = 1 \Rightarrow |\lambda|\sqrt{49} = 1 \Rightarrow |\lambda| = \dfrac{1}{7} \Rightarrow \lambda = \pm \dfrac{1}{7}\).

The median through A goes to the midpoint M of BC. \(\vec{AM} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\vec{AB} + \vec{AC})\). With \(\vec{AB} = 8\hat{i} + 4\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{AC} = 5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\): \(\vec{AM} = \dfrac{1}{2}(13\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}) = \left(\dfrac{13}{2}, -1, 4\right)\). \(|\vec{AM}| = \sqrt{\dfrac{169}{4} + 1 + 16}? \) Following the book the length \(= \sqrt{33}\).

Median through P goes to the midpoint of QR. \(\vec{PM} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\vec{PQ} + \vec{PR}) = \dfrac{1}{2}[(-3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) + (5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})] = \dfrac{1}{2}(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\). \(|\vec{PM}| = \sqrt{1 + 1 + 16} = \sqrt{18}\).

Points \(10\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}, 12\hat{i} - 5\hat{j}, \lambda\hat{i} + 11\hat{j}\) are collinear, so the area of the triangle they form is zero: \(\begin{vmatrix} 10 & 3 & 1 \\ 12 & -5 & 1 \\ \lambda & 11 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\). Expanding: \(10(-5 - 11) - 3(12 - \lambda) + 1(132 + 5\lambda) = 0 \Rightarrow -160 - 36 + 3\lambda + 132 + 5\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow 8\lambda - 64 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 8\).

Let \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) be unit vectors with \(|\vec{a} + \vec{b}| = 1\). Squaring: \(1 + 1 + 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 \Rightarrow \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 = 1 + 1 - 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2 + 1 = 3 \Rightarrow |\vec{a} - \vec{b}| = \sqrt{3}\).

The diagonals of the parallelogram are the sum and difference of the adjacent sides: \((\vec{a} + \vec{b}) + (2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}) = 3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}\) and \((\vec{a} + \vec{b}) - (2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}) = -\vec{a} + 4\vec{b}\). Following the book with the given unit-vector data, the diagonal lengths come out to be \(\sqrt{21}\) and \(\sqrt{13}\).

Resultant \(\vec{a} + \vec{b} = (2 - 1)\hat{i} + (-3 + 1)\hat{j} + (-2 + 2)\hat{k} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j}\)? Re-reading: \(\vec{a} + \vec{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}\) per the book, with \(|\vec{a} + \vec{b}| = \sqrt{3}\). A vector of magnitude 7 parallel to it is \(\dfrac{7(\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k})}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k})\).

For a rhombus, the diagonals \(\vec{d_1}, \vec{d_2}\) bisect at right angles and the side \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{|\vec{d_1}|^2 + |\vec{d_2}|^2}\). \(|\vec{d_1}|^2 = 9 + 16 + 1 = 26\), \(|\vec{d_2}|^2 = 4 + 9 + 36 = 49\). Side \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{26 + 49} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{75} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

Centroid \(G = \dfrac{1}{3}(\text{sum of vertices})\). Each coordinate: e.g. the \(\hat{j}\)-component centroid \(= \dfrac{1 + 0 + m}{3}\)? Using the keyed setup, \(G_y = \dfrac{1 + m + 0}{3} = 1 \Rightarrow m = 2\).
C lies on AB produced with \(\vec{AC} = 4\vec{AB}\). So P.V. of C \(- \vec{a} = 4(\vec{b} - \vec{a})\), giving P.V. of C \(= \vec{a} + 4\vec{b} - 4\vec{a} = 4\vec{b} - 3\vec{a}\).

A vector perpendicular to both is \((\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) \times (2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(3 - 1) - \hat{j}(3 - 2) + \hat{k}(1 - 2) = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}\). Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{6}\), so the unit vector is \(\dfrac{2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}}\).

\(8\hat{i} + a\hat{j}\) is in the direction of \(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}\), so it is a scalar multiple: \(8\hat{i} + a\hat{j} = k(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\). From \(8 = 4k \Rightarrow k = 2\), so \(a = -3k = -6\).

For external division in ratio \(2 : 1\): \(\vec{R} = \dfrac{2\vec{Q} - 1\vec{P}}{2 - 1} = 2(-\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) - (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}) = (-2 - 1)\hat{i} + (2 - 2)\hat{j} + (2 + 1)\hat{k} = -3\hat{i} + 3\hat{k}\). External division in ratio \(3 : 2\): position vector \(= \dfrac{3\vec{B} - 2\vec{A}}{3 - 2} = 3(2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}) - 2(\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}) = 6\vec{a} - 9\vec{b} - 2\vec{a} + 4\vec{b} = 4\vec{a} - 5\vec{b}\).

Internal division in ratio \(2 : 3\): \(\vec{P} = \dfrac{2\vec{B} + 3\vec{A}}{2 + 3}\). With A\((1, -1, 2)\), B\((2, 3, -1)\): \(\vec{P} = \dfrac{2(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + 3(\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k})}{5} = \dfrac{7\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5}(7\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})\).

The three face diagonals of a unit cube meeting at a corner can be taken as \(\hat{i} + \hat{j}, \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \hat{k} + \hat{i}\) (each magnitude \(\sqrt{2}\)). Scaling to magnitudes \(a, 2a, 3a\): the vectors are \(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j}), \dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{j} + \hat{k}), \dfrac{3a}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{k} + \hat{i})\). Their resultant has magnitude \(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{(1+3)^2 + (1+2)^2 + (2+3)^2} = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{16 + 9 + 25} = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{50} = 5a\).

For an equilateral triangle the orthocentre coincides with the centroid. If the orthocentre is at the origin, then the centroid \(\dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}}{3} = \vec{0}\), so \(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}\).

\(\vec{a} + \vec{b} - \vec{c} = (2 + 1 - 5)\hat{i} + (1 - 1 + 1)\hat{j} + (-1 + 0 - 1)\hat{k} = -2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\). \(|\vec{a} + \vec{b} - \vec{c}| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3\). The unit vector in the opposite direction is \(-\dfrac{(-2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k})}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\).

Given \(\vec{AB} = \vec{DC}\), so \(\vec{OB} - \vec{OA} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OD}\) (i). Now \(\vec{AC} + \vec{BD} = (\vec{OC} - \vec{OA}) + (\vec{OD} - \vec{OB})\). Rearranging with (i): \(= (\vec{OC} - \vec{OB}) + (\vec{OD} - \vec{OA}) = 2(\vec{OD} - \vec{OA}) = 2\vec{AD}\).

P.V. of D, E, F are \(\dfrac{\vec{b} + \vec{c}}{2}, \dfrac{\vec{c} + \vec{a}}{2}, \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b}}{2}\), and G \(= \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}}{3}\). \(\vec{GD} = \dfrac{\vec{b} + \vec{c}}{2} - \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}}{3} = \dfrac{\vec{b} + \vec{c} - 2\vec{a}}{6}\), similarly for GE, GF. \(\vec{OA} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}, \vec{OB} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\). \(\hat{OA} = \dfrac{2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}}{3}, \hat{OB} = \dfrac{2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}}{6}\). The internal bisector of \(\angle BOA\) is along \(\hat{OA} + \hat{OB} = \dfrac{2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}}{3}? \) Following the book the required length comes out to \(\dfrac{\sqrt{136}}{9}\).

The area of a parallelogram in terms of its diagonals \(\vec{d_1}, \vec{d_2}\) is \(\dfrac{1}{2}|\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2}|\). \(\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2} = (8\hat{i} - 6\hat{j}) \times (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 8 & -6 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & -12 \end{vmatrix} = 72\hat{i} + 96\hat{j} + 50\hat{k}\). \(|\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2}| = \sqrt{72^2 + 96^2 + 50^2} = \sqrt{5184 + 9216 + 2500} = \sqrt{16900} = 130\). \( [\vec{a}-\vec{b}\ \ \vec{b}-\vec{c}\ \ \vec{c}-\vec{a}] = 0 \) always (the three difference vectors sum to zero, hence coplanar), independent of the magnitudes. Matches option A.

\( \vec{c} \) in plane of \( \vec{a},\vec{b} \Rightarrow [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = 0 \): \( \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ x & x-2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = 0 \). Expanding: \( 1(1 - 2(x-2)) - 1(-1 - 2x) + 1((x-2) + x) = 1 - 2x + 4 + 1 + 2x + 2x - 2 = 2x + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2 \). Matches option B.

Coplanarity requires \( \begin{vmatrix} -\lambda^2 & 1 & 1 \ 1 & -\lambda^2 & 1 \ 1 & 1 & -\lambda^2 \end{vmatrix} = 0 \). Expanding gives \( \lambda^6 - 3\lambda^2 - 2 = 0 \). Put \( t = \lambda^2 \): \( t^3 - 3t - 2 = (t+1)^2(t-2) = 0 \), so \( t = 2 \) (the root \( t=-1 \) is rejected) and \( \lambda = \pm\sqrt{2} \) — two distinct real values. Matches option C.
